claims.text: A defect-inclusive first-principles and data-driven framework will predict the electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than analytical approaches based on perfect crystals.
Oxygen interstitials and associated vacancies are important defect states for predicting conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect-induced scattering becomes critical in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed hybrid approach combines ab initio calculations with machine-learning corrections.
Explicit oxygen-interstitial and vacancy modeling will improve on predictions obtained solely from defect-free analytical models.
Oxygen interstitials and vacancies provide additional electron-scattering channels.
Oxygen interstitials and vacancies modify phonon transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen impurities introduce localized scattering centers that enhance electron-phonon interactions.
Defect-mediated scattering reduces charge-carrier mobility relative to an ideal, defect-free crystal.
Traditional defect-free models systematically overestimate the conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The defect-inclusive model will predict lower electrical conductivity values that agree more closely with experiment.
Defect scattering will dominate in the 0–200 K regime and cause a more pronounced reduction in conductivity.
In the 300–1200 K regime, oxygen scattering will cause a moderate conductivity decrease relative to an ideal crystal.
Defect-free analytical predictions are less accurate when compared with measurements on specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach is intended to be applicable from 0 K to 1200 K for oxygen contents near 1 wt.%.
Accuracy may degrade above 1200 K or at oxygen concentrations substantially greater than 1 wt.%.
A prediction error greater than ±10% for oxygen-containing samples across the tested temperature regimes would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to outperform traditional defect-free predictions would falsify the claimed advantage.
